newsitem.title: GERMANY: SGL Carbon says faces U.S. lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: SGL Carbon says faces U.S. lawsuit.

text.p: Germany's SGL Carbon AG, being probed by U.S. and European Union officials on allegations of price-fixing for graphite electrodes, said Tuesday it faced a class-action lawsuit in the United States.
It said the suit, tied to allegations that it conspired with other makers to control market prices over the last five years, was without merit and that it would fight it.
SGL Carbon is the world's leading carbon and graphite maker, producing materials used in medical analysis and steel recyling.
Other companies named in the lawsuit, which SGL Carbon said was filed in Charlotte, N.C., were graphite electrode industry leader UCAR International and Carbide/Graphite Group Inc., SGL Carbon said.
No further details about the lawsuit were immediately available.

Shares in SGL Carbon, a darling of the German share market after it was spun off from chemical group Hoechst AG , ended bourse trade on Tuesday down 10.25 marks at 231.50 marks amid concerns about costs from the lawsuit.
Earlier this month, EU officials said they were investigating SGL and others in the graphite electrode industry, whose products are used to make steel.

A U.S. federal grand jury in Pennsylvania is reviewing allegations of price-fixing in the industry, which was burdened with major overcapacity in the 1980s that caused manufacturers to suffer large losses.
SGL Carbon was one of the companies to be born out of the industry consolidation.

Prices for the electrodes have still not reached the price per ton seen in the mid-1980s despite attempts to raise them due to higher costs for materials. Industry analysts have said profit margins remain low, making it hard for new competitors.
